title: Decline a card without leaking its number

blocks.text: Exception messages end up in logs and sometimes in responses, so they must not hold passwords, tokens or full card numbers. They should still say what failed, with which values. Write:

items: The checked `CardDeclinedException(String message, String lastFour)` with `getLastFour()`.

`Payments.authorize(String cardNumber, long amountCents, long limitCents)`: returns `"approved"` when the amount is within the limit, and otherwise throws `CardDeclinedException` with the message `Card ending <last four> declined: <amount> over limit <limit>` and the last four digits.

rows: throws `CardDeclinedException("Card ending 1111 declined: 5000 over limit 3000")`, `getLastFour()` is `"1111"`

blocks.text: Card numbers are at least four digits long here, and not all of them have 16. Be precise about what "within the limit" means.

cases.says: An amount within the limit is approved; one over it throws CardDeclinedException carrying the card's last four digits.
The message names only the last four digits and the amounts; the full card number never reaches a log.
An amount exactly at the limit is still approved.
The last four digits are counted from the end, so a 15-digit card shows its own last four.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: A message is written for the log's reader: what failed, with which values.
Exception messages reach logs, so they never hold passwords, tokens or full card numbers.
